workflow_runs.stop_reason — a vendor rejection now records tool_error_unrecoverable rather than worker_lost

migrationCompatibility.notes: No schema change. stop_reason values written are existing members of the CHECK constraint (tool_error_unrecoverable, llm_error, worker_lost); no new value is introduced, so no migration is needed and a code-only rollback is safe.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: redeploy the prior release; streams go back to hanging on failed runs and vendor errors go back to reading worker_lost, which is the current state

acceptanceCommands: PYTHONPATH=$PWD/backend/src python -m pytest tests -m 'not live and not demo_contract' -q
doNotInfer: Do not reuse PersistingEventSink.emit in the crash handler — it commits its own session, and the handler needs the event row, run status and card revert in ONE transaction. Share the publish helper instead.
Do not let a publish failure re-raise. The row is already committed; the handler's job is to stop a run being stranded non-terminal (#1210).
Do not put the exception classifier in workers — .importlinter.toml gives workers no edge to integrations at any depth.
Do not deep-import juli_backend.integrations.tiktok.exceptions; cross-package depth is capped at 2. Use the public package root.
Do not claim #1390 is fully closed. An unrecognised exception still records worker_lost as the residual bucket; a dedicated stop reason would need a migration and TS parity.
